name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1
lead: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 (Pal-GHK) is a synthetic lipopeptide made of the amino acids glycine, histidine and lysine joined to palmitic acid, used in cosmetic skincare. [2] It is marketed as a collagen-stimulating signal peptide and is one of the two peptides in the branded blend Matrixyl 3000. [1][2]

Grokipedia attributes its development to the French ingredient company Sederma around 2000, building on the GHK peptide reported in human plasma in 1973 (this account is from an AI-generated source). [2] Published evidence for wrinkle reduction in people is limited in the sources reviewed; recent papers are laboratory or permeation studies. [1][4]

paras: The palmitic acid chain is added to increase fat solubility and skin penetration. [2] The compound is commonly sold as a white powder and used in creams and serums. [2]

Manufacturers and reviews describe signal peptides as mimicking collagen breakdown fragments to prompt fibroblasts to make extracellular matrix. [2] A 2026 study examined collagen metabolism in skin fibroblasts and timed application of palmitoyl tripeptide-1 at night alongside baicalin by day. [5] A 2026 computational study screened cosmetic peptides for effects on type III collagen. [4]

In a 2026 study, serums containing palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 were applied to the skin of three volunteers and the stratum corneum analyzed; both peptides were detected in all layers with signal falling by depth, suggesting they remained largely between cells. [1]

No randomized trial of palmitoyl tripeptide-1 alone for wrinkles was found in the sources reviewed. Related work includes the circadian-timed fibroblast study and a registered trial of an AI-personalized skincare regimen for facial photoaging in 43 women, which is not specific to this peptide. [5][6]
US product labels list it in body creams, for example one regimen advising use of a cream three times a day with warnings for external use only and to discontinue if irritation occurs. [7]

timeline.event: GHK peptide identified in human plasma (reported by Grokipedia). [2]
Sederma launches Matrixyl, patents around this time (reported by Grokipedia). [2]

card.summary: The collagen-signal peptide half of Matrixyl 3000; widely used, with mostly lab and permeation data behind it.
card.note: Origin story comes largely from an AI-generated reference; human efficacy trials are sparse.

quick.overview:
Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 is a lab-made peptide (glycine-histidine-lysine plus a fatty acid) used in anti-wrinkle creams and serums. It is one of the two peptides in Matrixyl 3000.

Recent published work is mostly laboratory, permeation and computational studies; no dedicated wrinkle trial was found.
quick.mechanism: It is described as a signal peptide that prompts skin fibroblasts to make collagen and matrix. The fatty acid chain is meant to help it cross the skin barrier, though one study found the peptides stayed in the outer layer.
quick.risks: Product labels advise external use only, avoiding eyes, and stopping if irritation occurs. It is sold as a cosmetic ingredient.
